sections.content: Common present-tense actions are expressed with indefinite conjugation. Every regular verb follows the same six-person pattern -- *dolgozom* (I work), *dolgozol* (you work), *dolgozik* (he/she works), *dolgozunk* (we work), *dolgoztok* (you all work), *dolgoznak* (they work).

items.english: I always work in the morning.
We work together on the project.
Are you all working today too?

sections.content: The ending carries the person: -om/-öm (I), -ol/-el/-öl (you), -ik or nothing (he/she), -unk/-ünk (we), -tok/-tek/-tök (you all), -nak/-nek (they). Vowel harmony decides which variant fits the verb -- *dolgoz-* is a back-vowel stem, so it takes -unk, -tok, -nak; a front-vowel verb like *köszön* would take -ünk, -tek/-tök, -nek instead. You can often omit the subject pronoun since the ending already says who.
